beliefs: Every letter is replaced by its predecessor in the alphabet (a->z, b->a, ..., A->Z, B->A, ...) [E1, E9, E10]
A run of consecutive 'l'/'L' collapses to a single character [E2, E3, E5]
After collapsing, a run at a word start (start of string or after a non-letter) becomes 'k'/'K' [E2, E3, E6, E7]
A single 'l' after a letter is left as 'l' (not shifted) [E6, E8, E9, E10]
A single 'l' after a digit or space is left unchanged [E6, E8]
Case is preserved for all transformations [E1, E2, E3]
When a run of 2+ l's follows a letter, the output is predecessor(letter) + 'l' + (tail with its first character dropped) [E20, E21, E22, E23, E24]
The tail after a run of l's is everything after the run; its first character is dropped and the rest kept verbatim (no further shifting) [E18, E20, E24]
A single 'l' after a letter followed by a tail: the 'l' stays and the tail is kept verbatim (no dropping) [E10]
The 'l'/'L' handling is special-cased and does not follow the general predecessor shift [E2, E5, E9, E10]
notes: Key fix: when a run of 2+ l's follows a letter, output is predecessor(letter)+'l'+tail-with-first-char-dropped (E24 confirms drop-one, not drop-two). Single-l-after-letter keeps tail verbatim (E10: bla->ala).
